newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil slides, chasing futures.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil slides, chasing futures.

text.p: NWE high sulphur cracked fuel oil was weaker on Friday following Thursday's late futures sell-off but business was dampened by holidays in a number of European countries, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded at $114 or $114.50 fob ARA and remained relatively stable for much of the day.
High sulphur cargoes were weaker. A trader who bought a prompt Russian M-100 cargo on Thursday at $119-$120 cif NWE was heard trying to sell it again.
One utility player said he had been shown the cargo at $117/$118 a tonne, while a U.K. refiner had been offered it $1 lower than that. November cargo swaps were pegged at around $115/$116.
A large trader was heard having been awarded part of Turkey's latest high and low sulphur fuel oil tenders. No more details were immediately available.
Low sulphur fuel oil prices fell but later recovered, with November swaps talked around $119/$120 fob NWE by the day's end.
